answer: The V12-A structural gate checks three families. Identifiers: every V12 document must have valid strict frontmatter; volume, chapter and page identifiers must be unique; model, scenario, run and decision identifiers must be unique; and pattern identifiers must resolve in the existing registry. Links: every scenario model_id must resolve; every run model_id and scenario_id must resolve; every decision candidate run must resolve; every pattern identifier and owner page must resolve in the existing registry, including the owner document identifier and owner path. The reverse index must be derived from the records, not hand-edited. The iron rule also requires that no protected existing page or card outside V12 reference V12: the validator scans for V12 paths and V12-only identifiers, and a violation fails the gate. Hashes: every stored hash must match the current model or scenario file. Run records store model and scenario SHA-256 values (plus input and result hashes), and a change to either canonical input invalidates the run until it is regenerated. Existing cards and owner pages carry promotion hashes that must remain untouched; adding a V12 backlink would change a protected file and invalidate its records.
